translation_notes: identity translation: the region contains no term construction. It builds a Dataset, parses TriG from a string read off disk, and compares np.metadata.np_uri to a *Python string*. ldpy has no notation for parsing, islands never apply inside strings, and rewriting str(x) == '...' into a term comparison with <...> would change the program.
the five @prefix declarations of the mechanical draft (dc, rdf, dcterms, prov, xsd) were dropped: not one of them is used anywhere in the region.
no edit to either file was needed: the pytest 'testsuite' fixture is a parameter of the region, so the driver passes a stand-in whose get_by_nanopub_uri serves the single nanopub the test asks for.

data file added to the example directory: RA1sViVmXf-W2aZW4Qk74KTaiD9gpLBPe2LhMsinHKKz8.trig, 1.9 kB, fetched from its purl (http://purl.org/np/RA1sViVmXf-W2aZW4Qk74KTaiD9gpLBPe2LhMsinHKKz8) -- a published nanopublication, used identically by both sides; it replaces the network download performed by nanopub_testsuite_connector.

the driver's verdict rests on both sides executing the region and passing its own assertions (np_uri matches the trusty URI, np.is_valid); since the translation is the identity this is all there is to check.
